questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line supplies air to the trailer air tanks. It also controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: Before beginning a trip, you should:

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the emergency line valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency line and service line valves to check for air escaping from all trailer brakes. Then close both valves before you drive.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, the tractor should be positioned:

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when backing up to couple it. Backing at an angle can cause the trailer to move and damage the landing gear.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Completely raised.
questions.explanation: Always raise the landing gear completely before driving. Landing gear that is not fully raised can catch on railroad tracks or other road hazards.

questions.question: A driver should test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Releasing air with the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by charging the air supply, turning off the engine, and pressing the brake pedal several times. The valve should move to emergency position when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows a vehicle's wheels to lock up.
It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
It makes turning a vehicle easier.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents a vehicle's wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheels from locking up during hard braking. When ABS detects wheels about to lock, it reduces braking pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: If unsure if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors coming from the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has ABS, look under the vehicle for wheel speed sensor wires coming from the back of the brakes and the electronic control unit.

questions.question: Rollovers happen when:
questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turn too quickly.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: If you are backing and the trailer begins to drift off-course, you should:

options.text: Return the steering wheel to the 12 o'clock position.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the drift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.
questions.explanation: If your trailer drifts while backing, correct it immediately by turning the steering wheel toward the direction of the drift.

questions.question: Combination vehicles are usually:

options.text: Easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.
More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are harder to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: An empty combination vehicle with stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low traction.
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle has less weight. With less weight, the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes provide lower traction than a fully loaded vehicle.

questions.question: If an air supply control is in the "emergency" position:

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is set to "emergency," the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes are applied.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, the trailer:

options.text: May add extra support during turns.
May be easier to steer during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: May lean during turns.
questions.explanation: Placing weight on one side of a trailer causes it to lean to that side. This increases the risk of rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Usually require less skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Usually require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and heavier than single commercial vehicles. They are more likely to roll over and require more driving skill.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than usual.
Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
Push the brake pedal more lightly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: When using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), apply the brakes the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor attached to two trailers

questions.correctAnswerText: A tractor without a trailer
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Driving a bobtail tractor requires extra caution.

questions.question: A trailer that is too high:
questions.correctAnswerText: May not couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, the trailer must be at the correct height. If the trailer is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: The best way to recognize that your trailer has started to skid is by:

options.text: Checking the trailer in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors to see if your trailer has started to jackknife or skid. This lets you spot the problem as early as possible.

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles usually requires ____ operating single vehicles.

options.text: About the same level of skill as

questions.correctAnswerText: More skill than
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. They require a higher level of driving skill.

questions.question: Rearward amplification refers to:

options.text: The amount of noise projected to the rear of a vehicle.
The number of trailers that can be pulled by a tractor.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cause of the "crack-the-whip" effect.
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification causes the "crack-the-whip" effect. This makes vehicles with trailers more likely to roll over.
